verses.sanskrit: दोषधातुमला मूलं सदा देहस्य तं चलः। उत्साहोच्छ्वासनिश्वासचेष्टावेगप्रवर्तनैः॥१॥
verses.student_meaning: Doshas, dhatus and malas are the fundamental supports of the body; normal Vata promotes enthusiasm, respiration, movement, natural urges, proper tissue movement and sensory function.

verses.sanskrit: सम्यग्गत्या च धातूनामक्षाणां पाटवेन च। अनुगृह्णात्यविकृतः, पित्तं पक्त्यूष्मदर्शनैः॥२॥
verses.student_meaning: Normal Vata supports proper tissue movement and sensory acuity; normal Pitta supports digestion, heat and visual function.

verses.sanskrit: क्षुत्तृड्रुचिप्रभामेधाधीशौर्यतनुमार्दवैः। श्लेष्मा स्थिरत्वस्निग्धत्वसन्धिबन्धक्षमादिभिः॥३॥
verses.student_meaning: Normal Pitta supports appetite, thirst, taste, complexion, intellect, courage and bodily softness; Kapha supports stability, unctuousness, joint binding and endurance.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीणनं जीवनं लेपः स्नेहो धारणपूरणे। गर्भोत्पादश्च धातूनां श्रेष्ठं कर्म क्रमात्स्मृतम्॥४॥
verses.student_meaning: The principal sequential functions of the seven dhatus are nourishment, life-support, structural coating, unctuousness, support, filling and reproduction.

verses.sanskrit: अवष्टम्भः पुरीषस्य, मूत्रस्य क्लेदवाहनम्। स्वेदस्य क्लेदविधृतिः वृद्धस्तु कुरुतेऽनिलः॥५॥
verses.student_meaning: The chief functions of faeces, urine and sweat are respectively bodily support, removal of fluid waste and regulation/retention of moisture; increased Vata produces characteristic disturbances.

verses.sanskrit: कार्श्यकार्ष्ण्योष्णकामित्वकम्पानाहशकृद्ग्रहान्। बलनिद्रेन्द्रियभ्रंशप्रलापभ्रमदीनताः॥६॥
verses.student_meaning: Excess Vata produces emaciation, dark complexion, heat-seeking tendency, tremor, abdominal distension, constipation, weakness, sleep and sensory disturbance, delirium, dizziness and debility.

verses.sanskrit: पीतविण्मूत्रनेत्रत्वक्क्षुत्तृड्दाहाल्पनिद्रताः। पित्तम् श्लेष्माऽग्निसदनप्रसेकालस्यगौरवम्॥७॥
verses.student_meaning: Excess Pitta produces yellow discoloration, altered stool and urine, ocular and skin changes, thirst, burning and reduced sleep; the verse then begins the description of increased Kapha.

verses.sanskrit: श्वैत्यशैत्यश्लथाङ्गत्वं श्वासकासातिनिद्रताः। रसोऽपि श्लेष्मवत् रक्तं विसर्पप्लीहविद्रधीन्॥८॥
verses.student_meaning: Excess Kapha produces pallor, coldness, laxity, dyspnoea, cough and excessive sleep; increased Rasa produces disorders resembling increased Kapha, while increased Rakta produces swelling and suppurative conditions.

verses.sanskrit: कुष्ठवातास्रपित्तास्रगुल्मोपकुशकामलाः। व्यङ्गाग्निनाशसम्मोहरक्तत्वङ्‌नेत्रमूत्रताः॥९॥
verses.student_meaning: Rakta increase may manifest through skin, inflammatory, metabolic and ocular/urinary disorders including visarpa, splenic enlargement, abscess, skin disease, jaundice and complexion changes.

verses.sanskrit: मांसं गण्डार्बुदग्रन्थिगण्डोरूदरवृद्धिताः। कण्ठादिष्वधिमांसं च तद्वन्मेदस्तथा श्रमम्॥१०॥
verses.student_meaning: Increased Mamsa produces excessive tissue masses and enlargements; increased Medas produces comparable excess tissue burden and fatigue.

verses.sanskrit: अल्पेऽपि चेष्टिते श्वासं स्फिक्स्तनोदरलम्बनम्। अस्थ्यध्यस्थ्यधिदंतांश्च मज्जा नेत्राङ्गगौरवम्॥११॥
verses.student_meaning: Excess Mamsa/Medas may cause breathlessness with little exertion and hanging of buttocks, breasts or abdomen; increased Asthi and Majja produce dental, skeletal, ocular and bodily heaviness-related changes.

verses.sanskrit: पर्वसु स्थूलमूलानि कुर्यात्कृच्छ्राण्यरूंषि च। अतिस्त्रीकामतां वृद्धं शुक्रं शुक्राश्मरीमपि॥१२॥
verses.student_meaning: Increased Asthi may produce hard-rooted lesions around joints; increased Shukra may manifest as excessive sexual desire and seminal calculi.

verses.sanskrit: कुक्षावाध्मानमाटोपं गौरवं वेदनां शकृत्। मूत्रं तु बस्तिनिस्तोदं कृतेऽप्यकृतसंज्ञताम्॥१३॥
verses.student_meaning: Increased Purisha causes abdominal distension, rumbling, heaviness and pain; increased urine produces bladder discomfort and abnormal urinary sensation.

verses.sanskrit: स्वेदोऽतिस्वेददौर्गन्ध्यकण्डूः एवं च लक्षयेत्। दूषिकादीनपि मलान् बाहुल्यगुरुतादिभिः॥१४॥
verses.student_meaning: Excess sweat produces excessive sweating, odour and itching; other minor malas show excess through increased quantity, heaviness and related signs.

verses.sanskrit: लिङ्गं क्षीणेऽनिलेऽङ्गस्य सादोऽल्पं भाषितेहितम्। संज्ञामोहस्तथा श्लेष्मवृद्ध्युक्तामयसम्भवः॥१५॥
verses.student_meaning: Vata depletion causes bodily weakness, reduced speech and activity, and cognitive disturbance; the verse also notes disorders associated with Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: पित्ते मन्दोऽनलः शीतं प्रभाहानिः कफे भ्रमः। श्लेष्माशयानां शून्यत्वं हृद्द्रवः श्लथसन्धिता॥१६॥
verses.student_meaning: Pitta depletion causes weak digestion, coldness and loss of complexion; Kapha depletion produces dizziness, emptiness of Kapha sites, cardiac fluidity and lax joints.

verses.sanskrit: रसे रौक्ष्यं श्रमः शोषो ग्लानिः शब्दासहिष्णुता। रक्तेऽम्लशिशिरप्रीतिशिराशैथिल्यरूक्षताः॥१७॥
verses.student_meaning: Rasa depletion produces dryness, fatigue, wasting, lassitude and reduced tolerance of sound; Rakta depletion produces preference for sour/cold factors, lax veins and dryness.

verses.sanskrit: मांसेऽक्षग्लानिगण्डस्फिक्शुष्कतासन्धिवेदनाः। मेदसि स्वपनं कट्याः प्लीह्नो वृद्धिः कृशाङ्गता॥१८॥
verses.student_meaning: Mamsa depletion produces eye fatigue, wasting of cheeks and buttocks and joint pain; Medas depletion produces wasting and related enlargement/alteration around the spleen region.

verses.sanskrit: अस्थन्यस्थितोदः शदनं दन्तकेशनखादिषु। अस्थनं मज्जनि सौषिर्यं भ्रमस्तिमिरदर्शनम्॥१९॥
verses.student_meaning: Asthi depletion produces pain and weakness of teeth, hair and nails; Majja depletion produces hollow feeling of bones, dizziness and visual darkness.

verses.sanskrit: शुक्रे चिरात् प्रसिच्येत शुक्रं शोणितमेव वा। तोदोऽत्यर्थं वृषणयोर्मेढ्रं धूमायतीव च॥२०॥
verses.student_meaning: Shukra depletion produces delayed or scanty ejaculation, possible blood admixture, severe testicular pain and a burning or smoke-like penile sensation.

verses.sanskrit: पुरीषे वायुरन्त्राणि सशब्दो वेष्टयन्निव। कुक्षौ भ्रमति यात्यूर्ध्वं हृत्पार्श्वे पीडयन् भृशम्॥२१॥
verses.student_meaning: Purisha disturbance with depletion produces abnormal Vata movement in the intestines, abdominal rumbling and upward movement causing severe cardiac and flank pain.

verses.sanskrit: मूत्रेऽल्पं मूत्रयेत्कृच्छ्राद्विवर्णं सास्त्रमेव वा। स्वेदे रोमच्युतिः स्तब्धरोमता स्फुटनं त्वचः॥२२॥
verses.student_meaning: Urine depletion causes scanty, difficult and discoloured urination that may be blood-tinged; sweat depletion causes hair loss, rigid hair follicles and skin fissuring.

verses.sanskrit: मलानामतिसूक्ष्माणां दुर्लक्ष्यं लक्षयेत् क्षयम्। स्वमलायनसंशोषतोदशून्यत्वलाघवैः॥२३॥
verses.student_meaning: Subtle mala depletion may be difficult to detect and is inferred from drying and pain of their channels, emptiness and lightness.

verses.sanskrit: दोषादीनां यथास्वं च विद्याद्वृद्धिक्षयौ भिषक्। क्षयेण विपरीतानां गुणानां वर्धनेन च॥२४॥
verses.student_meaning: The physician should recognize increase and decrease of doshas and related factors by observing opposite or increased qualities respectively.

verses.sanskrit: वृद्धिं मलानां सङ्गाच्च क्षयं चाति विसर्गतः। मलोचितत्वाद्देहस्य क्षयो वृद्धेस्तु पीडनः॥२५॥
verses.student_meaning: Mala increases mainly through retention/accumulation and decreases through excessive elimination; depletion can disturb normal bodily adaptation, while excess causes distress.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रास्थिनि स्थितो वायुः, पित्तं तु स्वेदरक्तयोः। श्लेष्मा शेषेषु, तेनैषामाश्रयाश्रयिणां मिथः॥२६॥
verses.student_meaning: Vata primarily resides in Asthi, Pitta in sweat and blood, and Kapha in the remaining sites; these form mutually related support-supporter relationships.

verses.sanskrit: यदेकस्य तदन्यस्य वर्धनक्षपणौषधम्। अस्थिमारुतयोर्नैवं, प्रायो वृद्धिर्हि तर्पणात्॥२७॥
verses.student_meaning: In general, the increase or decrease of one factor can be used to influence its related factor, but the Vata-Asthi relationship is an important exception; nourishment commonly increases tissue.

verses.sanskrit: श्लेष्मणाऽनुगता तस्मात् सङ्क्षयस्तद्विपर्ययात्। वायुनाऽनुगतोऽस्माच्च वृद्धिक्षयसमुद्भवान्॥२८॥
verses.student_meaning: Kapha follows its associated tissue relationship in depletion and its reverse in the corresponding increase/decrease pattern; Vata similarly participates in the disorders arising from increase or decrease.

verses.sanskrit: विकारान् साधयेच्छीघ्रं क्रमाल्लङ्घनबृंहणैः। वायोरन्यत्र, तज्जांस्तु तैरेवोत्क्रमयोजितैः॥२९॥
verses.student_meaning: Dosha- and dhatu-related disorders are managed promptly with Langhana or Brimhana in the appropriate sequence; Vata-related disorders require the opposite ordering.

verses.sanskrit: विशेषाद्रक्तवृद्ध्युत्थान् रक्तस्रुतिविरेचनैः। मांसवृद्धिभवान् रोगान् शस्त्रक्षाराग्निकर्मभिः॥३०॥
verses.student_meaning: Disorders from increased Rakta are addressed with bloodletting and purgation; disorders from excessive Mamsa are addressed with classical surgical, alkaline and cauterizing measures.

verses.sanskrit: स्थौल्यकार्श्योपचारेण मेदोजानस्थिसङ्क्षयात्। जातान् क्षीरघृतैस्तिक्तसंयुतैर्बस्तिभिस्तथा॥३१॥
verses.student_meaning: Meda-related disorders are addressed through obesity/emaciation management; disorders associated with Asthi depletion are described with milk, ghee, bitter drugs and appropriate basti measures.

verses.sanskrit: विड्वृद्धिजानतीसारक्रियया, विट्‌क्षयोद्भवान्। मेषाजमध्यकुल्माषयवमाषद्वयादिभिः॥३२॥
verses.student_meaning: Disorders from excess faeces are managed with measures for diarrhoea; depletion is addressed with nourishing dietary examples such as meat, pulses and cereals.

verses.sanskrit: मूत्रवृद्धिक्षयोत्थांश्च मेहकृच्छ्रचिकित्सया। व्यायामाभ्यञ्जनस्वेदमद्यैः स्वेदक्षयोद्भवान्॥३३॥
verses.student_meaning: Urine excess/depletion is managed according to urinary disorders; sweat depletion is addressed through exercise, oiling, sudation and appropriate fermented preparations.

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्थानस्थस्य कायाग्नेरंशा धातुषु संश्रिताः। तेषां सादातिदीप्तिभ्यां धातुवृद्धिक्षयोद्भवः॥३४॥
verses.student_meaning: Fractions of the body fire associated with the main digestive fire are distributed in the dhatus; impairment or excessive activity of these tissue fires produces dhatu increase or depletion.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वो धातुः परं कुर्याद्वृद्धः क्षीणश्च तद्विधम्। दोषा दुष्टा रसैर्धातून् दूषयन्त्युभये मलान्॥३५॥
verses.student_meaning: Each preceding dhatu nourishes the succeeding one when increased or depleted; vitiated doshas through rasa disturb dhatus and both may disturb the malas.

verses.sanskrit: अधो द्वे, सप्त शिरसि, खानि स्वेदवहानि च। मला मलायनानि स्युर्यथास्वं तेष्वतो गदाः॥३६॥
verses.student_meaning: The principal mala channels include two inferior outlets, seven head openings and sweat-bearing channels; diseases arise according to the particular mala and its pathway.

verses.sanskrit: ओजस्तु तेजो धातूनां शुक्रान्तानां परं स्मृतम्। हृदयस्थमपि व्यापि देहस्थितिनिबन्धनम्॥३७॥
verses.student_meaning: Ojas is regarded as the supreme essence of the dhatus up to Shukra; although located in the heart, it pervades the body and sustains bodily existence.

verses.sanskrit: स्निग्धं सोमात्मकं शुद्धमीषल्लोहितपीतकम्। यन्नाशे नियतं नाशो यस्मिंस्तिष्ठति तिष्ठति॥३८॥
verses.student_meaning: Ojas is described as unctuous, soma-dominant, pure and slightly reddish-yellow; its loss is associated with loss of life, while its presence sustains life.

verses.sanskrit: निष्पद्यन्ते यतो भावा विविधा देहसंश्रयाः। ओजः क्षीयेत कोपक्षुद्ध्यानशोकश्रमादिभिः॥३९॥
verses.student_meaning: From Ojas arise diverse states that support the body; it is depleted by anger, hunger, worry, grief, exertion and similar factors.

verses.sanskrit: बिभेति दुर्बलोऽभीक्ष्णं ध्यायति व्यथितेन्द्रियः। दुःच्छायो दुर्मना रूक्षो भवेत्क्षामश्च तत्क्षये॥४०॥
verses.student_meaning: With Ojas depletion a person becomes fearful, weak, repeatedly worried, distressed in the senses, mentally low, dry and emaciated.

verses.sanskrit: जीवनीयौषधक्षीररसाद्यास्तत्र भेषजम्। ओजोवृद्धौ हि देहस्य तुष्टिपुष्टिबलोदयः॥४१॥
verses.student_meaning: Rejuvenative medicines, milk and nourishing preparations are described as measures for Ojas; increasing Ojas supports satisfaction, nourishment and strength.

verses.sanskrit: यदन्नं द्वेष्टि यदपि प्रार्थयेताविरोधि तु। तत्तत्त्यजन् समश्नंश्च तौ तौ वृद्धिक्षयौ जयेत्॥४२॥
verses.student_meaning: Food that is disliked should be avoided, while desired food that is not incompatible may be taken appropriately to help manage dosha increase or depletion.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्वते हि रुचिं दोषा विपरीतसमानयोः। वृद्धाः क्षीणाश्च भूयिष्ठं लक्षयन्त्यबुधास्तु न॥४३॥
verses.student_meaning: Increased doshas generally create attraction toward opposite qualities, while depleted doshas tend to create attraction toward similar qualities; an unwise person may fail to recognize this.

verses.sanskrit: यथाबलं यथास्वं च दोषा वृद्धा वितन्वते। रूपाणि, जहति क्षीणाः, समाः स्वं कर्म कुर्वते॥४४॥
verses.student_meaning: Increased doshas express their characteristic signs according to strength; depleted doshas lose their usual manifestations, while balanced doshas perform their normal functions.

verses.sanskrit: य एव देहस्य समा विवृद्ध्यै त एव दोषा विषमा वधाय। यस्मादतस्ते हितचर्ययैव क्षयाद्विवृद्धेरिव रक्षणीयाः॥४५॥
verses.student_meaning: The same doshas that support bodily growth when balanced become causes of destruction when disturbed; therefore appropriate conduct should protect them from both depletion and excess.

learning_outcomes: Define dosha, dhatu and mala as fundamental components of the body.
Explain the normal functions of Vata, Pitta and Kapha.
Describe principal functions of the seven dhatus and three major malas.
Recognize classical signs of dosha, dhatu and mala increase and depletion.
Explain Ashraya-Ashrayi relationships and their clinical implications.
Explain the role of tissue-level Agni in dhatu increase and depletion.
Describe Ojas, its qualities, depletion causes, manifestations and restorative measures.
Apply the final principles of dosha balance, dietary desire and appropriate conduct.
exam_focus: Normal functions of Vata, Pitta and Kapha.
Dosha, dhatu and mala vriddhi/kshaya lakshana.
Ojas: nature, location, depletion and management.
Verse 44 on increased, depleted and balanced doshas.
Verse 45 on protection from both dosha depletion and excess.

revision_summary: Memorize the normal functions of Vata, Pitta and Kapha.
Create separate tables for dosha, dhatu and mala vriddhi/kshaya signs.
Understand the Ashraya-Ashrayi relationship rather than memorizing it as an isolated list.
Revise the management principles in verses 29-36.
Learn Ojas qualities, causes of depletion, manifestations and restorative measures.
Use verses 42-45 to connect diet, dosha desire, balance and preventive conduct.
